s1.syndrome_frame: Abdominal pain and adnexal mass with chronic unilateral lower limb edema
salient_findings: Non-pitting edema of the left leg extending to the labia majora
Firm, non-tender, mobile mass in the right lower quadrant
key_facts: 1-month history of insidious-onset right lower abdominal pain
Lifelong non-pitting edema of the left leg
Regular menses
No tobacco or alcohol use
Afebrile, blood pressure 110/80 mmHg, pulse 88 beats/min
Respiratory rate 16 breaths/min, oxygen saturation 98% on room air
Cardiac and respiratory examinations were unremarkable
Neurologic exam was normal
Abdomen revealed a firm, non-tender, mobile mass measuring approximately 12 cm × 10 cm
Bimanual pelvic examination confirmed a right adnexal mass
Normal baseline hematologic, biochemical, thyroid, renal, and HIV/HBV/HCV serologies
Tumor markers within reference range
Pap smear was negative
Transvaginal ultrasound showed multiple uterine fibroids and a large hypoechoic lesion in the right adnexa

shortlist.label: Ovarian cystadenocarcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Concerning imaging findings for an ovarian neoplasm and presence of a large adnexal mass

shortlist.label: Mucinous cystadenocarcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Type of ovarian cancer that can present with a large abdominal mass

shortlist.label: Serous cystadenocarcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Most common type of ovarian cancer, can present with abdominal pain and adnexal mass

shortlist.label: Ovarian teratoma
shortlist.why_kept: Can cause abdominal pain and adnexal mass, although less likely given the patient's age and tumor markers

shortlist.label: Ovarian fibroma
shortlist.why_kept: Can cause abdominal pain and adnexal mass, and is a possible diagnosis given the patient's symptoms and normal tumor markers

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with a large, solid-cystic lesion in the right adnexa, as seen on transvaginal ultrasound and CT, along with the concern for an ovarian neoplasm based on imaging findings, supports this diagnosis. Although tumor markers were normal, the imaging characteristics and the presence of a large adnexal mass are consistent with ovarian cystadenocarcinoma.

rejected.label: Mucinous cystadenocarcinoma
rejected.why: While possible, the diagnosis is not specifically supported by the mucinous type without further histological evidence.

rejected.label: Serous cystadenocarcinoma
rejected.why: Similar to mucinous cystadenocarcinoma, the specific type of serous is not indicated by the provided information.

rejected.label: Ovarian teratoma
rejected.why: Typically presents with more varied tissue types within the tumor and often at a younger age, which does not perfectly match this patient's presentation.

rejected.label: Ovarian fibroma
rejected.why: These are typically solid, benign tumors that do not usually present with the cystic components seen in this patient's imaging.
